Date
April 02, 2026

Editor
Łukasz Langa

This article explains the new features in Python 3.9, compared to 3.8. Python 3.9 was released on October 5th, 2020.

For full details, see the [changelog](link_0).

See also

[**PEP 596**](link_1) - Python 3.9 Release Schedule

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   a number of standard library modules ([`audioop`](link_10), [`ast`](link_15), [`grp`](link_16), `_hashlib`, [`pwd`](link_17), `_posixsubprocess`, [`random`](link_18), [`select`](link_19), [`struct`](link_20), [`termios`](link_21), [`zlib`](link_22)) are now using the stable ABI defined by PEP 384.

New library modules:

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   an implementation of a topological sort of a graph is now provided in the new [`graphlib`](link_58) module.

Release process changes:

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

## You should check for DeprecationWarning in your code[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#you-should-check-for-deprecationwarning-in-your-code "Permalink to this headline")

When Python 2.7 was still supported, a lot of functionality in Python 3 was kept for backward compatibility with Python 2.7. With the end of Python 2 support, these backward compatibility layers have been removed, or will be removed soon. Most of them emitted a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) warning for several years. For example, using `collections.Mapping` instead of `collections.abc.Mapping` emits a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) since Python 3.3, released in 2012.

Test your application with the [`-W`](link_27)`default` command-line option to see [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) and [`PendingDeprecationWarning`](link_26), or even with [`-W`](link_27)`error` to treat them as errors. [Warnings Filter](link_28) can be used to ignore warnings from third-party code.

Python 3.9 is the last version providing those Python 2 backward compatibility layers, to give more time to Python projects maintainers to organize the removal of the Python 2 support and add support for Python 3.9.

Aliases to [Abstract Base Classes](link_29) in the [`collections`](link_30) module, like `collections.Mapping` alias to [`collections.abc.Mapping`](link_29), are kept for one last release for backward compatibility. They will be removed from Python 3.10.

More generally, try to run your tests in the [Python Development Mode](link_31) which helps to prepare your code to make it compatible with the next Python version.

Note: a number of pre-existing deprecations were removed in this version of Python as well. Consult the [Removed](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#removed-in-python-39) section.

## New Features[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-features "Permalink to this headline")

### Dictionary Merge & Update Operators[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#dictionary-merge-update-operators "Permalink to this headline")

Merge (`|`) and update (`|=`) operators have been added to the built-in [`dict`](link_45) class. Those complement the existing `dict.update` and `{**d1, **d2}` methods of merging dictionaries.

Example:

>>> x = {"key1": "value1 from x", "key2": "value2 from x"}
>>> y = {"key2": "value2 from y", "key3": "value3 from y"}
>>> x | y
{'key1': 'value1 from x', 'key2': 'value2 from y', 'key3': 'value3 from y'}
>>> y | x
{'key2': 'value2 from x', 'key3': 'value3 from y', 'key1': 'value1 from x'}

See [**PEP 584**](link_2) for a full description. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-36144](link_32).)

### New String Methods to Remove Prefixes and Suffixes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-string-methods-to-remove-prefixes-and-suffixes "Permalink to this headline")

[`str.removeprefix(prefix)`](link_45) and [`str.removesuffix(suffix)`](link_45) have been added to easily remove an unneeded prefix or a suffix from a string. Corresponding `bytes`, `bytearray`, and `collections.UserString` methods have also been added. See [**PEP 616**](link_5) for a full description. (Contributed by Dennis Sweeney in [bpo-39939](link_33).)

### Type Hinting Generics in Standard Collections[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#type-hinting-generics-in-standard-collections "Permalink to this headline")

In type annotations you can now use built-in collection types such as `list` and `dict` as generic types instead of importing the corresponding capitalized types (e.g. `List` or `Dict`) from `typing`. Some other types in the standard library are also now generic, for example `queue.Queue`.

Example:

def greet_all(names: list[str]) -> None:
    for name in names:
        print("Hello", name)

See [**PEP 585**](link_3) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Ethan Smith, and Batuhan Taşkaya in [bpo-39481](link_34).)

### New Parser[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-parser "Permalink to this headline")

Python 3.9 uses a new parser, based on [PEG](link_35) instead of [LL(1)](link_36). The new parser’s performance is roughly comparable to that of the old parser, but the PEG formalism is more flexible than LL(1) when it comes to designing new language features. We’ll start using this flexibility in Python 3.10 and later.

The [`ast`](link_15) module uses the new parser and produces the same AST as the old parser.

In Python 3.10, the old parser will be deleted and so will all functionality that depends on it (primarily the [`parser`](link_37) module, which has long been deprecated). In Python 3.9 _only_, you can switch back to the LL(1) parser using a command line switch (
```
-X
oldparser
```
) or an environment variable (`PYTHONOLDPARSER=1`).

See [**PEP 617**](link_8) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Pablo Galindo and Lysandros Nikolaou in [bpo-40334](link_38).)

## Other Language Changes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#other-language-changes "Permalink to this headline")

*   [`__import__()`](link_39) now raises [`ImportError`](link_26) instead of [`ValueError`](link_26), which used to occur when a relative import went past its top-level package. (Contributed by Ngalim Siregar in [bpo-37444](link_40).)

*   Python now gets the absolute path of the script filename specified on the command line (ex: `python3 script.py`): the `__file__` attribute of the [`__main__`](link_41) module became an absolute path, rather than a relative path. These paths now remain valid after the current directory is changed by [`os.chdir()`](link_42). As a side effect, the traceback also displays the absolute path for [`__main__`](link_41) module frames in this case. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-20443](link_43).)

*   In the [Python Development Mode](link_31) and in debug build, the _encoding_ and _errors_ arguments are now checked for string encoding and decoding operations. Examples: [`open()`](link_39), [`str.encode()`](link_45) and [`bytes.decode()`](link_45).

By default, for best performance, the _errors_ argument is only checked at the first encoding/decoding error and the _encoding_ argument is sometimes ignored for empty strings. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-37388](link_44).)

*   `"".replace("", s, n)` now returns `s` instead of an empty string for all non-zero `n`. It is now consistent with `"".replace("", s)`. There are similar changes for [`bytes`](link_45) and [`bytearray`](link_45) objects. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-28029](link_46).)

*   Any valid expression can now be used as a [decorator](link_47). Previously, the grammar was much more restrictive. See [**PEP 614**](link_4) for details. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-39702](link_48).)

*   Improved help for the [`typing`](link_49) module. Docstrings are now shown for all special forms and special generic aliases (like `Union` and `List`). Using [`help()`](link_39) with generic alias like `List[int]` will show the help for the correspondent concrete type (`list` in this case). (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40257](link_50).)

*   Parallel running of [`aclose()`](link_51) / [`asend()`](link_51) / [`athrow()`](link_51) is now prohibited, and `ag_running` now reflects the actual running status of the async generator. (Contributed by Yury Selivanov in [bpo-30773](link_52).)

*   Unexpected errors in calling the `__iter__` method are no longer masked by `TypeError` in the [`in`](link_51) operator and functions [`contains()`](link_12), [`indexOf()`](link_12) and [`countOf()`](link_12) of the [`operator`](link_12) module. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40824](link_53).)

*   Unparenthesized lambda expressions can no longer be the expression part in an `if` clause in comprehensions and generator expressions. See [bpo-41848](link_54) and [bpo-43755](link_55) for details.

## New Modules[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-modules "Permalink to this headline")

### zoneinfo[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#zoneinfo "Permalink to this headline")

The [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module brings support for the IANA time zone database to the standard library. It adds [`zoneinfo.ZoneInfo`](link_24), a concrete [`datetime.tzinfo`](link_56) implementation backed by the system’s time zone data.

Example:

>>> from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
>>> from datetime import datetime, timedelta

>>> # Daylight saving time
>>> dt = datetime(2020, 10, 31, 12, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/Los_Angeles"))
>>> print(dt)
2020-10-31 12:00:00-07:00
>>> dt.tzname()
'PDT'

>>> # Standard time
>>> dt += timedelta(days=7)
>>> print(dt)
2020-11-07 12:00:00-08:00
>>> print(dt.tzname())

Release

Date
April 02, 2026

Editor
Łukasz Langa

This article explains the new features in Python 3.9, compared to 3.8. Python 3.9 was released on October 5th, 2020.

For full details, see the [changelog](link_0).

See also

[**PEP 596**](link_1) - Python 3.9 Release Schedule

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   a number of standard library modules ([`audioop`](link_10), [`ast`](link_15), [`grp`](link_16), `_hashlib`, [`pwd`](link_17), `_posixsubprocess`, [`random`](link_18), [`select`](link_19), [`struct`](link_20), [`termios`](link_21), [`zlib`](link_22)) are now using the stable ABI defined by PEP 384.

New library modules:

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   an implementation of a topological sort of a graph is now provided in the new [`graphlib`](link_58) module.

Release process changes:

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

## You should check for DeprecationWarning in your code[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#you-should-check-for-deprecationwarning-in-your-code "Permalink to this headline")

When Python 2.7 was still supported, a lot of functionality in Python 3 was kept for backward compatibility with Python 2.7. With the end of Python 2 support, these backward compatibility layers have been removed, or will be removed soon. Most of them emitted a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) warning for several years. For example, using `collections.Mapping` instead of `collections.abc.Mapping` emits a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) since Python 3.3, released in 2012.

Test your application with the [`-W`](link_27)`default` command-line option to see [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) and [`PendingDeprecationWarning`](link_26), or even with [`-W`](link_27)`error` to treat them as errors. [Warnings Filter](link_28) can be used to ignore warnings from third-party code.

Python 3.9 is the last version providing those Python 2 backward compatibility layers, to give more time to Python projects maintainers to organize the removal of the Python 2 support and add support for Python 3.9.

Aliases to [Abstract Base Classes](link_29) in the [`collections`](link_30) module, like `collections.Mapping` alias to [`collections.abc.Mapping`](link_29), are kept for one last release for backward compatibility. They will be removed from Python 3.10.

More generally, try to run your tests in the [Python Development Mode](link_31) which helps to prepare your code to make it compatible with the next Python version.

Note: a number of pre-existing deprecations were removed in this version of Python as well. Consult the [Removed](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#removed-in-python-39) section.

## New Features[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-features "Permalink to this headline")

### Dictionary Merge & Update Operators[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#dictionary-merge-update-operators "Permalink to this headline")

Merge (`|`) and update (`|=`) operators have been added to the built-in [`dict`](link_45) class. Those complement the existing `dict.update` and `{**d1, **d2}` methods of merging dictionaries.

Example:

>>> x = {"key1": "value1 from x", "key2": "value2 from x"}
>>> y = {"key2": "value2 from y", "key3": "value3 from y"}
>>> x | y
{'key1': 'value1 from x', 'key2': 'value2 from y', 'key3': 'value3 from y'}
>>> y | x
{'key2': 'value2 from x', 'key3': 'value3 from y', 'key1': 'value1 from x'}

See [**PEP 584**](link_2) for a full description. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-36144](link_32).)

### New String Methods to Remove Prefixes and Suffixes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-string-methods-to-remove-prefixes-and-suffixes "Permalink to this headline")

[`str.removeprefix(prefix)`](link_45) and [`str.removesuffix(suffix)`](link_45) have been added to easily remove an unneeded prefix or a suffix from a string. Corresponding `bytes`, `bytearray`, and `collections.UserString` methods have also been added. See [**PEP 616**](link_5) for a full description. (Contributed by Dennis Sweeney in [bpo-39939](link_33).)

### Type Hinting Generics in Standard Collections[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#type-hinting-generics-in-standard-collections "Permalink to this headline")

In type annotations you can now use built-in collection types such as `list` and `dict` as generic types instead of importing the corresponding capitalized types (e.g. `List` or `Dict`) from `typing`. Some other types in the standard library are also now generic, for example `queue.Queue`.

Example:

def greet_all(names: list[str]) -> None:
    for name in names:
        print("Hello", name)

See [**PEP 585**](link_3) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Ethan Smith, and Batuhan Taşkaya in [bpo-39481](link_34).)

### New Parser[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-parser "Permalink to this headline")

Python 3.9 uses a new parser, based on [PEG](link_35) instead of [LL(1)](link_36). The new parser’s performance is roughly comparable to that of the old parser, but the PEG formalism is more flexible than LL(1) when it comes to designing new language features. We’ll start using this flexibility in Python 3.10 and later.

The [`ast`](link_15) module uses the new parser and produces the same AST as the old parser.

```
-X
oldparser
```
) or an environment variable (`PYTHONOLDPARSER=1`).

See [**PEP 617**](link_8) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Pablo Galindo and Lysandros Nikolaou in [bpo-40334](link_38).)

*   `"".replace("", s, n)` now returns `s` instead of an empty string for all non-zero `n`. It is now consistent with `"".replace("", s)`. There are similar changes for [`bytes`](link_45) and [`bytearray`](link_45) objects. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-28029](link_46).)

*   Any valid expression can now be used as a [decorator](link_47). Previously, the grammar was much more restrictive. See [**PEP 614**](link_4) for details. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-39702](link_48).)

*   Improved help for the [`typing`](link_49) module. Docstrings are now shown for all special forms and special generic aliases (like `Union` and `List`). Using [`help()`](link_39) with generic alias like `List[int]` will show the help for the correspondent concrete type (`list` in this case). (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40257](link_50).)

Release
3.9.25

Date
April 02, 2026

Editor
Łukasz Langa

This article explains the new features in Python 3.9, compared to 3.8. Python 3.9 was released on October 5th, 2020.

For full details, see the [changelog](link_0).

See also

[**PEP 596**](link_1) - Python 3.9 Release Schedule

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   a number of standard library modules ([`audioop`](link_10), [`ast`](link_15), [`grp`](link_16), `_hashlib`, [`pwd`](link_17), `_posixsubprocess`, [`random`](link_18), [`select`](link_19), [`struct`](link_20), [`termios`](link_21), [`zlib`](link_22)) are now using the stable ABI defined by PEP 384.

New library modules:

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   an implementation of a topological sort of a graph is now provided in the new [`graphlib`](link_58) module.

Release process changes:

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

## You should check for DeprecationWarning in your code[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#you-should-check-for-deprecationwarning-in-your-code "Permalink to this headline")

When Python 2.7 was still supported, a lot of functionality in Python 3 was kept for backward compatibility with Python 2.7. With the end of Python 2 support, these backward compatibility layers have been removed, or will be removed soon. Most of them emitted a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) warning for several years. For example, using `collections.Mapping` instead of `collections.abc.Mapping` emits a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) since Python 3.3, released in 2012.

Test your application with the [`-W`](link_27)`default` command-line option to see [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) and [`PendingDeprecationWarning`](link_26), or even with [`-W`](link_27)`error` to treat them as errors. [Warnings Filter](link_28) can be used to ignore warnings from third-party code.

Python 3.9 is the last version providing those Python 2 backward compatibility layers, to give more time to Python projects maintainers to organize the removal of the Python 2 support and add support for Python 3.9.

Aliases to [Abstract Base Classes](link_29) in the [`collections`](link_30) module, like `collections.Mapping` alias to [`collections.abc.Mapping`](link_29), are kept for one last release for backward compatibility. They will be removed from Python 3.10.

More generally, try to run your tests in the [Python Development Mode](link_31) which helps to prepare your code to make it compatible with the next Python version.

Note: a number of pre-existing deprecations were removed in this version of Python as well. Consult the [Removed](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#removed-in-python-39) section.

## New Features[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-features "Permalink to this headline")

### Dictionary Merge & Update Operators[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#dictionary-merge-update-operators "Permalink to this headline")

Merge (`|`) and update (`|=`) operators have been added to the built-in [`dict`](link_45) class. Those complement the existing `dict.update` and `{**d1, **d2}` methods of merging dictionaries.

Example:

>>> x = {"key1": "value1 from x", "key2": "value2 from x"}
>>> y = {"key2": "value2 from y", "key3": "value3 from y"}
>>> x | y
{'key1': 'value1 from x', 'key2': 'value2 from y', 'key3': 'value3 from y'}
>>> y | x
{'key2': 'value2 from x', 'key3': 'value3 from y', 'key1': 'value1 from x'}

See [**PEP 584**](link_2) for a full description. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-36144](link_32).)

### New String Methods to Remove Prefixes and Suffixes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-string-methods-to-remove-prefixes-and-suffixes "Permalink to this headline")

[`str.removeprefix(prefix)`](link_45) and [`str.removesuffix(suffix)`](link_45) have been added to easily remove an unneeded prefix or a suffix from a string. Corresponding `bytes`, `bytearray`, and `collections.UserString` methods have also been added. See [**PEP 616**](link_5) for a full description. (Contributed by Dennis Sweeney in [bpo-39939](link_33).)

### Type Hinting Generics in Standard Collections[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#type-hinting-generics-in-standard-collections "Permalink to this headline")

In type annotations you can now use built-in collection types such as `list` and `dict` as generic types instead of importing the corresponding capitalized types (e.g. `List` or `Dict`) from `typing`. Some other types in the standard library are also now generic, for example `queue.Queue`.

Example:

def greet_all(names: list[str]) -> None:
    for name in names:
        print("Hello", name)

See [**PEP 585**](link_3) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Ethan Smith, and Batuhan Taşkaya in [bpo-39481](link_34).)

### New Parser[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-parser "Permalink to this headline")

Python 3.9 uses a new parser, based on [PEG](link_35) instead of [LL(1)](link_36). The new parser’s performance is roughly comparable to that of the old parser, but the PEG formalism is more flexible than LL(1) when it comes to designing new language features. We’ll start using this flexibility in Python 3.10 and later.

The [`ast`](link_15) module uses the new parser and produces the same AST as the old parser.

In Python 3.10, the old parser will be deleted and so will all functionality that depends on it (primarily the [`parser`](link_37) module, which has long been deprecated). In Python 3.9 _only_, you can switch back to the LL(1) parser using a command line switch (
```
-X
oldparser
```
) or an environment variable (`PYTHONOLDPARSER=1`).

See [**PEP 617**](link_8) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Pablo Galindo and Lysandros Nikolaou in [bpo-40334](link_38).)

## Other Language Changes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#other-language-changes "Permalink to this headline")

*   [`__import__()`](link_39) now raises [`ImportError`](link_26) instead of [`ValueError`](link_26), which used to occur when a relative import went past its top-level package. (Contributed by Ngalim Siregar in [bpo-37444](link_40).)

*   Python now gets the absolute path of the script filename specified on the command line (ex: `python3 script.py`): the `__file__` attribute of the [`__main__`](link_41) module became an absolute path, rather than a relative path. These paths now remain valid after the current directory is changed by [`os.chdir()`](link_42). As a side effect, the traceback also displays the absolute path for [`__main__`](link_41) module frames in this case. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-20443](link_43).)

*   In the [Python Development Mode](link_31) and in debug build, the _encoding_ and _errors_ arguments are now checked for string encoding and decoding operations. Examples: [`open()`](link_39), [`str.encode()`](link_45) and [`bytes.decode()`](link_45).

By default, for best performance, the _errors_ argument is only checked at the first encoding/decoding error and the _encoding_ argument is sometimes ignored for empty strings. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-37388](link_44).)

*   `"".replace("", s, n)` now returns `s` instead of an empty string for all non-zero `n`. It is now consistent with `"".replace("", s)`. There are similar changes for [`bytes`](link_45) and [`bytearray`](link_45) objects. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-28029](link_46).)

*   Any valid expression can now be used as a [decorator](link_47). Previously, the grammar was much more restrictive. See [**PEP 614**](link_4) for details. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-39702](link_48).)

*   Improved help for the [`typing`](link_49) module. Docstrings are now shown for all special forms and special generic aliases (like `Union` and `List`). Using [`help()`](link_39) with generic alias like `List[int]` will show the help for the correspondent concrete type (`list` in this case). (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40257](link_50).)

*   Parallel running of [`aclose()`](link_51) / [`asend()`](link_51) / [`athrow()`](link_51) is now prohibited, and `ag_running` now reflects the actual running status of the async generator. (Contributed by Yury Selivanov in [bpo-30773](link_52).)

*   Unexpected errors in calling the `__iter__` method are no longer masked by `TypeError` in the [`in`](link_51) operator and functions [`contains()`](link_12), [`indexOf()`](link_12) and [`countOf()`](link_12) of the [`operator`](link_12) module. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40824](link_53).)

*   Unparenthesized lambda expressions can no longer be the expression part in an `if` clause in comprehensions and generator expressions. See [bpo-41848](link_54) and [bpo-43755](link_55) for details.

## New Modules[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-modules "Permalink to this headline")

### zoneinfo[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#zoneinfo "Permalink to this headline")

The [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module brings support for the IANA time zone database to the standard library. It adds [`zoneinfo.ZoneInfo`](link_24), a concrete [`datetime.tzinfo`](link_56) implementation backed by the system’s time zone data.

Example:

>>> from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
>>> from datetime import datetime, timedelta

>>> # Daylight saving time
>>> dt = datetime(2020, 10, 31, 12, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/Los_Angeles"))
>>> print(dt)
2020-10-31 12:00:00-07:00
>>> dt.tzname()
'PDT'

>>> # Standard time
>>> dt += timedelta(days=7)
>>> print(dt)
2020-11-07 12:00:00-08:00
>>> print(dt.tzname())
PST

*   [`__import__()`](link_39) now raises [`ImportError`](link_26) instead of [`ValueError`](link_26), which used to occur when a relative import went past its top-level package. (Contributed by Ngalim Siregar in [bpo-37444](link_40).)

### zoneinfo[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#zoneinfo "Permalink to this headline")

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   a number of standard library modules ([`audioop`](link_10), [`ast`](link_15), [`grp`](link_16), `_hashlib`, [`pwd`](link_17), `_posixsubprocess`, [`random`](link_18), [`select`](link_19), [`struct`](link_20), [`termios`](link_21), [`zlib`](link_22)) are now using the stable ABI defined by PEP 384.

New library modules:

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   an implementation of a topological sort of a graph is now provided in the new [`graphlib`](link_58) module.

Release process changes:

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

## You should check for DeprecationWarning in your code[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#you-should-check-for-deprecationwarning-in-your-code "Permalink to this headline")

When Python 2.7 was still supported, a lot of functionality in Python 3 was kept for backward compatibility with Python 2.7. With the end of Python 2 support, these backward compatibility layers have been removed, or will be removed soon. Most of them emitted a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) warning for several years. [Warnings Filter](link_28) can be used to ignore warnings from third-party code.

Python 3.9 is the last version providing those Python 2 backward compatibility layers, to give more time to Python projects maintainers to organize the removal of the Python 2 support and add support for Python 3.9.

Aliases to [Abstract Base Classes](link_29) in the [`collections`](link_30) module, like `collections.Mapping` alias to [`collections.abc.Mapping`](link_29), are kept for one last release for backward compatibility. They will be removed from Python 3.10.

More generally, try to run your tests in the [Python Development Mode](link_31) which helps to prepare your code to make it compatible with the next Python version.

Example:

>>> y = {"key2": "value2 from y", "key3": "value3 from y"}
>>> x | y

Release
3.9.25

Date
April 02, 2026

Editor
Łukasz Langa

This article explains the new features in Python 3.9, compared to 3.8. Python 3.9 was released on October 5th, 2020.

For full details, see the [changelog](link_0).

See also

[**PEP 596**](link_1) - Python 3.9 Release Schedule

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   a number of standard library modules ([`audioop`](link_10), [`ast`](link_15), [`grp`](link_16), `_hashlib`, [`pwd`](link_17), `_posixsubprocess`, [`random`](link_18), [`select`](link_19), [`struct`](link_20), [`termios`](link_21), [`zlib`](link_22)) are now using the stable ABI defined by PEP 384.

New library modules:

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   an implementation of a topological sort of a graph is now provided in the new [`graphlib`](link_58) module.

Release process changes:

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

## You should check for DeprecationWarning in your code[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#you-should-check-for-deprecationwarning-in-your-code "Permalink to this headline")

When Python 2.7 was still supported, a lot of functionality in Python 3 was kept for backward compatibility with Python 2.7. With the end of Python 2 support, these backward compatibility layers have been removed, or will be removed soon. Most of them emitted a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) warning for several years. For example, using `collections.Mapping` instead of `collections.abc.Mapping` emits a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) since Python 3.3, released in 2012.

Test your application with the [`-W`](link_27)`default` command-line option to see [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) and [`PendingDeprecationWarning`](link_26), or even with [`-W`](link_27)`error` to treat them as errors. [Warnings Filter](link_28) can be used to ignore warnings from third-party code.

Python 3.9 is the last version providing those Python 2 backward compatibility layers, to give more time to Python projects maintainers to organize the removal of the Python 2 support and add support for Python 3.9.

Aliases to [Abstract Base Classes](link_29) in the [`collections`](link_30) module, like `collections.Mapping` alias to [`collections.abc.Mapping`](link_29), are kept for one last release for backward compatibility. They will be removed from Python 3.10.

More generally, try to run your tests in the [Python Development Mode](link_31) which helps to prepare your code to make it compatible with the next Python version.

Note: a number of pre-existing deprecations were removed in this version of Python as well. Consult the [Removed](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#removed-in-python-39) section.

## New Features[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-features "Permalink to this headline")

### Dictionary Merge & Update Operators[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#dictionary-merge-update-operators "Permalink to this headline")

Merge (`|`) and update (`|=`) operators have been added to the built-in [`dict`](link_45) class. Those complement the existing `dict.update` and `{**d1, **d2}` methods of merging dictionaries.

Example:

>>> x = {"key1": "value1 from x", "key2": "value2 from x"}
>>> y = {"key2": "value2 from y", "key3": "value3 from y"}
>>> x | y
{'key1': 'value1 from x', 'key2': 'value2 from y', 'key3': 'value3 from y'}
>>> y | x
{'key2': 'value2 from x', 'key3': 'value3 from y', 'key1': 'value1 from x'}

See [**PEP 584**](link_2) for a full description. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-36144](link_32).)

### New String Methods to Remove Prefixes and Suffixes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-string-methods-to-remove-prefixes-and-suffixes "Permalink to this headline")

[`str.removeprefix(prefix)`](link_45) and [`str.removesuffix(suffix)`](link_45) have been added to easily remove an unneeded prefix or a suffix from a string. Corresponding `bytes`, `bytearray`, and `collections.UserString` methods have also been added. See [**PEP 616**](link_5) for a full description. (Contributed by Dennis Sweeney in [bpo-39939](link_33).)

### Type Hinting Generics in Standard Collections[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#type-hinting-generics-in-standard-collections "Permalink to this headline")

In type annotations you can now use built-in collection types such as `list` and `dict` as generic types instead of importing the corresponding capitalized types (e.g. `List` or `Dict`) from `typing`. Some other types in the standard library are also now generic, for example `queue.Queue`.

Example:

def greet_all(names: list[str]) -> None:
    for name in names:
        print("Hello", name)

See [**PEP 585**](link_3) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Ethan Smith, and Batuhan Taşkaya in [bpo-39481](link_34).)

### New Parser[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-parser "Permalink to this headline")

Python 3.9 uses a new parser, based on [PEG](link_35) instead of [LL(1)](link_36). The new parser’s performance is roughly comparable to that of the old parser, but the PEG formalism is more flexible than LL(1) when it comes to designing new language features. We’ll start using this flexibility in Python 3.10 and later.

The [`ast`](link_15) module uses the new parser and produces the same AST as the old parser.

In Python 3.10, the old parser will be deleted and so will all functionality that depends on it (primarily the [`parser`](link_37) module, which has long been deprecated). In Python 3.9 _only_, you can switch back to the LL(1) parser using a command line switch (
```
-X
oldparser
```
) or an environment variable (`PYTHONOLDPARSER=1`).

See [**PEP 617**](link_8) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Pablo Galindo and Lysandros Nikolaou in [bpo-40334](link_38).)

## Other Language Changes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#other-language-changes "Permalink to this headline")

*   [`__import__()`](link_39) now raises [`ImportError`](link_26) instead of [`ValueError`](link_26), which used to occur when a relative import went past its top-level package. (Contributed by Ngalim Siregar in [bpo-37444](link_40).)

*   Python now gets the absolute path of the script filename specified on the command line (ex: `python3 script.py`): the `__file__` attribute of the [`__main__`](link_41) module became an absolute path, rather than a relative path. These paths now remain valid after the current directory is changed by [`os.chdir()`](link_42). As a side effect, the traceback also displays the absolute path for [`__main__`](link_41) module frames in this case. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-20443](link_43).)

*   In the [Python Development Mode](link_31) and in debug build, the _encoding_ and _errors_ arguments are now checked for string encoding and decoding operations. Examples: [`open()`](link_39), [`str.encode()`](link_45) and [`bytes.decode()`](link_45).

By default, for best performance, the _errors_ argument is only checked at the first encoding/decoding error and the _encoding_ argument is sometimes ignored for empty strings. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-37388](link_44).)

*   `"".replace("", s, n)` now returns `s` instead of an empty string for all non-zero `n`. It is now consistent with `"".replace("", s)`. There are similar changes for [`bytes`](link_45) and [`bytearray`](link_45) objects. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-28029](link_46).)

*   Any valid expression can now be used as a [decorator](link_47). Previously, the grammar was much more restrictive. See [**PEP 614**](link_4) for details. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-39702](link_48).)

*   Improved help for the [`typing`](link_49) module. Docstrings are now shown for all special forms and special generic aliases (like `Union` and `List`). Using [`help()`](link_39) with generic alias like `List[int]` will show the help for the correspondent concrete type (`list` in this case). (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40257](link_50).)

*   Parallel running of [`aclose()`](link_51) / [`asend()`](link_51) / [`athrow()`](link_51) is now prohibited, and `ag_running` now reflects the actual running status of the async generator. (Contributed by Yury Selivanov in [bpo-30773](link_52).)

*   Unexpected errors in calling the `__iter__` method are no longer masked by `TypeError` in the [`in`](link_51) operator and functions [`contains()`](link_12), [`indexOf()`](link_12) and [`countOf()`](link_12) of the [`operator`](link_12) module. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40824](link_53).)

*   Unparenthesized lambda expressions can no longer be the expression part in an `if` clause in comprehensions and generator expressions. See [bpo-41848](link_54) and [bpo-43755](link_55) for details.

## New Modules[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-modules "Permalink to this headline")

>>> # Standard time

2020-11-07 12:00:00-08:00
>>> print(dt.tzname())

*   [`__import__()`](link_39) now raises [`ImportError`](link_26) instead of [`ValueError`](link_26), which used to occur when a relative import went past its top-level package. (Contributed by Ngalim Siregar in [bpo-37444](link_40).)

### zoneinfo[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#zoneinfo "Permalink to this headline")

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

## New Modules[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-modules "Permalink to this headline")
### zoneinfo[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#zoneinfo "Permalink to this headline")
The [`zoneinfo`](https://docs.python.org/3.9/library/zoneinfo.html#module-zoneinfo "zoneinfo: IANA time zone support") module brings support for the IANA time zone database to the standard library. It adds [`zoneinfo.ZoneInfo`](https://docs.python.org/3.9/library/zoneinfo.html#zoneinfo.ZoneInfo "zoneinfo.ZoneInfo"), a concrete [`datetime.tzinfo`](https://docs.python.org/3.9/library/datetime.html#datetime.tzinfo "datetime.tzinfo") implementation backed by the system’s time zone data.
Example:
>>> from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo  
>>> from datetime import datetime, timedelta
>>> # Daylight saving time  
>>> dt = datetime(2020, 10, 31, 12, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("America/Los_Angeles"))  
>>> print(dt)  
2020-10-31 12:00:00-07:00  
>>> dt.tzname()  
'PDT'
>>> # Standard time  
>>> dt += timedelta(days=7)  
>>> print(dt)  
2020-11-07 12:00:00-08:00  
>>> print(dt.tzname())  
PST
As a fall-back source of data for platforms that don’t ship the IANA database, the [`tzdata`](https://pypi.org/project/tzdata/) module was released as a first-party package – distributed via PyPI and maintained by the CPython core team.
See also
[**PEP 615**](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0615) – Support for the IANA Time Zone Database in the Standard Library  
PEP written and implemented by Paul Ganssle

Release
3.9.25

Date
April 02, 2026

Editor
Łukasz Langa

This article explains the new features in Python 3.9, compared to 3.8. Python 3.9 was released on October 5th, 2020.

For full details, see the [changelog](link_0).

See also

[**PEP 596**](link_1) - Python 3.9 Release Schedule

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   a number of standard library modules ([`audioop`](link_10), [`ast`](link_15), [`grp`](link_16), `_hashlib`, [`pwd`](link_17), `_posixsubprocess`, [`random`](link_18), [`select`](link_19), [`struct`](link_20), [`termios`](link_21), [`zlib`](link_22)) are now using the stable ABI defined by PEP 384.

New library modules:

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   an implementation of a topological sort of a graph is now provided in the new [`graphlib`](link_58) module.

Release process changes:

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

## You should check for DeprecationWarning in your code[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#you-should-check-for-deprecationwarning-in-your-code "Permalink to this headline")

When Python 2.7 was still supported, a lot of functionality in Python 3 was kept for backward compatibility with Python 2.7. With the end of Python 2 support, these backward compatibility layers have been removed, or will be removed soon. Most of them emitted a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) warning for several years. For example, using `collections.Mapping` instead of `collections.abc.Mapping` emits a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) since Python 3.3, released in 2012.

Test your application with the [`-W`](link_27)`default` command-line option to see [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) and [`PendingDeprecationWarning`](link_26), or even with [`-W`](link_27)`error` to treat them as errors. [Warnings Filter](link_28) can be used to ignore warnings from third-party code.

Python 3.9 is the last version providing those Python 2 backward compatibility layers, to give more time to Python projects maintainers to organize the removal of the Python 2 support and add support for Python 3.9.

Aliases to [Abstract Base Classes](link_29) in the [`collections`](link_30) module, like `collections.Mapping` alias to [`collections.abc.Mapping`](link_29), are kept for one last release for backward compatibility. They will be removed from Python 3.10.

More generally, try to run your tests in the [Python Development Mode](link_31) which helps to prepare your code to make it compatible with the next Python version.

Note: a number of pre-existing deprecations were removed in this version of Python as well. Consult the [Removed](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#removed-in-python-39) section.

## New Features[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-features "Permalink to this headline")

### Dictionary Merge & Update Operators[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#dictionary-merge-update-operators "Permalink to this headline")

Merge (`|`) and update (`|=`) operators have been added to the built-in [`dict`](link_45) class. Those complement the existing `dict.update` and `{**d1, **d2}` methods of merging dictionaries.

Example:

>>> x = {"key1": "value1 from x", "key2": "value2 from x"}
>>> y = {"key2": "value2 from y", "key3": "value3 from y"}
>>> x | y
{'key1': 'value1 from x', 'key2': 'value2 from y', 'key3': 'value3 from y'}
>>> y | x
{'key2': 'value2 from x', 'key3': 'value3 from y', 'key1': 'value1 from x'}

See [**PEP 584**](link_2) for a full description. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-36144](link_32).)

### New String Methods to Remove Prefixes and Suffixes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-string-methods-to-remove-prefixes-and-suffixes "Permalink to this headline")

[`str.removeprefix(prefix)`](link_45) and [`str.removesuffix(suffix)`](link_45) have been added to easily remove an unneeded prefix or a suffix from a string. Corresponding `bytes`, `bytearray`, and `collections.UserString` methods have also been added. See [**PEP 616**](link_5) for a full description. (Contributed by Dennis Sweeney in [bpo-39939](link_33).)

### Type Hinting Generics in Standard Collections[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#type-hinting-generics-in-standard-collections "Permalink to this headline")

In type annotations you can now use built-in collection types such as `list` and `dict` as generic types instead of importing the corresponding capitalized types (e.g. `List` or `Dict`) from `typing`. Some other types in the standard library are also now generic, for example `queue.Queue`.

Example:

def greet_all(names: list[str]) -> None:
    for name in names:
        print("Hello", name)

See [**PEP 585**](link_3) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Ethan Smith, and Batuhan Taşkaya in [bpo-39481](link_34).)

### New Parser[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-parser "Permalink to this headline")

Python 3.9 uses a new parser, based on [PEG](link_35) instead of [LL(1)](link_36). The new parser’s performance is roughly comparable to that of the old parser, but the PEG formalism is more flexible than LL(1) when it comes to designing new language features. We’ll start using this flexibility in Python 3.10 and later.

The [`ast`](link_15) module uses the new parser and produces the same AST as the old parser.

In Python 3.10, the old parser will be deleted and so will all functionality that depends on it (primarily the [`parser`](link_37) module, which has long been deprecated). In Python 3.9 _only_, you can switch back to the LL(1) parser using a command line switch (
```
-X
oldparser
```
) or an environment variable (`PYTHONOLDPARSER=1`).

See [**PEP 617**](link_8) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Pablo Galindo and Lysandros Nikolaou in [bpo-40334](link_38).)

## Other Language Changes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#other-language-changes "Permalink to this headline")

*   [`__import__()`](link_39) now raises [`ImportError`](link_26) instead of [`ValueError`](link_26), which used to occur when a relative import went past its top-level package. (Contributed by Ngalim Siregar in [bpo-37444](link_40).)

*   Python now gets the absolute path of the script filename specified on the command line (ex: `python3 script.py`): the `__file__` attribute of the [`__main__`](link_41) module became an absolute path, rather than a relative path. These paths now remain valid after the current directory is changed by [`os.chdir()`](link_42). As a side effect, the traceback also displays the absolute path for [`__main__`](link_41) module frames in this case. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-20443](link_43).)

*   In the [Python Development Mode](link_31) and in debug build, the _encoding_ and _errors_ arguments are now checked for string encoding and decoding operations. Examples: [`open()`](link_39), [`str.encode()`](link_45) and [`bytes.decode()`](link_45).

By default, for best performance, the _errors_ argument is only checked at the first encoding/decoding error and the _encoding_ argument is sometimes ignored for empty strings. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-37388](link_44).)

*   `"".replace("", s, n)` now returns `s` instead of an empty string for all non-zero `n`. It is now consistent with `"".replace("", s)`. There are similar changes for [`bytes`](link_45) and [`bytearray`](link_45) objects. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-28029](link_46).)

*   Any valid expression can now be used as a [decorator](link_47). Previously, the grammar was much more restrictive. See [**PEP 614**](link_4) for details. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-39702](link_48).)

*   Improved help for the [`typing`](link_49) module. Docstrings are now shown for all special forms and special generic aliases (like `Union` and `List`). Using [`help()`](link_39) with generic alias like `List[int]` will show the help for the correspondent concrete type (`list` in this case). (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40257](link_50).)

*   Parallel running of [`aclose()`](link_51) / [`asend()`](link_51) / [`athrow()`](link_51) is now prohibited, and `ag_running` now reflects the actual running status of the async generator. (Contributed by Yury Selivanov in [bpo-30773](link_52).)

*   Unexpected errors in calling the `__iter__` method are no longer masked by `TypeError` in the [`in`](link_51) operator and functions [`contains()`](link_12), [`indexOf()`](link_12) and [`countOf()`](link_12) of the [`operator`](link_12) module. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40824](link_53).)

*   Unparenthesized lambda expressions can no longer be the expression part in an `if` clause in comprehensions and generator expressions. See [bpo-41848](link_54) and [bpo-43755](link_55) for details.

## New Modules[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-modules "Permalink to this headline")

*   [`__import__()`](link_39) now raises [`ImportError`](link_26) instead of [`ValueError`](link_26), which used to occur when a relative import went past its top-level package. (Contributed by Ngalim Siregar in [bpo-37444](link_40).)

### zoneinfo[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#zoneinfo "Permalink to this headline")

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

Release
3.9.25

Date
April 02, 2026

Editor
Łukasz Langa

This article explains the new features in Python 3.9, compared to 3.8. Python 3.9 was released on October 5th, 2020.

For full details, see the [changelog](link_0).

See also

[**PEP 596**](link_1) - Python 3.9 Release Schedule

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   a number of standard library modules ([`audioop`](link_10), [`ast`](link_15), [`grp`](link_16), `_hashlib`, [`pwd`](link_17), `_posixsubprocess`, [`random`](link_18), [`select`](link_19), [`struct`](link_20), [`termios`](link_21), [`zlib`](link_22)) are now using the stable ABI defined by PEP 384.

New library modules:

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   an implementation of a topological sort of a graph is now provided in the new [`graphlib`](link_58) module.

Release process changes:

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

## You should check for DeprecationWarning in your code[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#you-should-check-for-deprecationwarning-in-your-code "Permalink to this headline")

When Python 2.7 was still supported, a lot of functionality in Python 3 was kept for backward compatibility with Python 2.7. With the end of Python 2 support, these backward compatibility layers have been removed, or will be removed soon. Most of them emitted a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) warning for several years. For example, using `collections.Mapping` instead of `collections.abc.Mapping` emits a [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) since Python 3.3, released in 2012.

Test your application with the [`-W`](link_27)`default` command-line option to see [`DeprecationWarning`](link_26) and [`PendingDeprecationWarning`](link_26), or even with [`-W`](link_27)`error` to treat them as errors. [Warnings Filter](link_28) can be used to ignore warnings from third-party code.

Python 3.9 is the last version providing those Python 2 backward compatibility layers, to give more time to Python projects maintainers to organize the removal of the Python 2 support and add support for Python 3.9.

Aliases to [Abstract Base Classes](link_29) in the [`collections`](link_30) module, like `collections.Mapping` alias to [`collections.abc.Mapping`](link_29), are kept for one last release for backward compatibility. They will be removed from Python 3.10.

More generally, try to run your tests in the [Python Development Mode](link_31) which helps to prepare your code to make it compatible with the next Python version.

Note: a number of pre-existing deprecations were removed in this version of Python as well. Consult the [Removed](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#removed-in-python-39) section.

## New Features[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-features "Permalink to this headline")

### Dictionary Merge & Update Operators[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#dictionary-merge-update-operators "Permalink to this headline")

Merge (`|`) and update (`|=`) operators have been added to the built-in [`dict`](link_45) class. Those complement the existing `dict.update` and `{**d1, **d2}` methods of merging dictionaries.

Example:

>>> x = {"key1": "value1 from x", "key2": "value2 from x"}
>>> y = {"key2": "value2 from y", "key3": "value3 from y"}
>>> x | y
{'key1': 'value1 from x', 'key2': 'value2 from y', 'key3': 'value3 from y'}
>>> y | x
{'key2': 'value2 from x', 'key3': 'value3 from y', 'key1': 'value1 from x'}

See [**PEP 584**](link_2) for a full description. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-36144](link_32).)

### New String Methods to Remove Prefixes and Suffixes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-string-methods-to-remove-prefixes-and-suffixes "Permalink to this headline")

[`str.removeprefix(prefix)`](link_45) and [`str.removesuffix(suffix)`](link_45) have been added to easily remove an unneeded prefix or a suffix from a string. Corresponding `bytes`, `bytearray`, and `collections.UserString` methods have also been added. See [**PEP 616**](link_5) for a full description. (Contributed by Dennis Sweeney in [bpo-39939](link_33).)

### Type Hinting Generics in Standard Collections[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#type-hinting-generics-in-standard-collections "Permalink to this headline")

In type annotations you can now use built-in collection types such as `list` and `dict` as generic types instead of importing the corresponding capitalized types (e.g. `List` or `Dict`) from `typing`. Some other types in the standard library are also now generic, for example `queue.Queue`.

Example:

def greet_all(names: list[str]) -> None:
    for name in names:
        print("Hello", name)

See [**PEP 585**](link_3) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Ethan Smith, and Batuhan Taşkaya in [bpo-39481](link_34).)

### New Parser[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-parser "Permalink to this headline")

Python 3.9 uses a new parser, based on [PEG](link_35) instead of [LL(1)](link_36). The new parser’s performance is roughly comparable to that of the old parser, but the PEG formalism is more flexible than LL(1) when it comes to designing new language features. We’ll start using this flexibility in Python 3.10 and later.

The [`ast`](link_15) module uses the new parser and produces the same AST as the old parser.

In Python 3.10, the old parser will be deleted and so will all functionality that depends on it (primarily the [`parser`](link_37) module, which has long been deprecated). In Python 3.9 _only_, you can switch back to the LL(1) parser using a command line switch (
```
-X
oldparser
```
) or an environment variable (`PYTHONOLDPARSER=1`).

See [**PEP 617**](link_8) for more details. (Contributed by Guido van Rossum, Pablo Galindo and Lysandros Nikolaou in [bpo-40334](link_38).)

## Other Language Changes[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#other-language-changes "Permalink to this headline")

*   [`__import__()`](link_39) now raises [`ImportError`](link_26) instead of [`ValueError`](link_26), which used to occur when a relative import went past its top-level package. (Contributed by Ngalim Siregar in [bpo-37444](link_40).)

*   Python now gets the absolute path of the script filename specified on the command line (ex: `python3 script.py`): the `__file__` attribute of the [`__main__`](link_41) module became an absolute path, rather than a relative path. These paths now remain valid after the current directory is changed by [`os.chdir()`](link_42). As a side effect, the traceback also displays the absolute path for [`__main__`](link_41) module frames in this case. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-20443](link_43).)

*   In the [Python Development Mode](link_31) and in debug build, the _encoding_ and _errors_ arguments are now checked for string encoding and decoding operations. Examples: [`open()`](link_39), [`str.encode()`](link_45) and [`bytes.decode()`](link_45).

By default, for best performance, the _errors_ argument is only checked at the first encoding/decoding error and the _encoding_ argument is sometimes ignored for empty strings. (Contributed by Victor Stinner in [bpo-37388](link_44).)

*   `"".replace("", s, n)` now returns `s` instead of an empty string for all non-zero `n`. It is now consistent with `"".replace("", s)`. There are similar changes for [`bytes`](link_45) and [`bytearray`](link_45) objects. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-28029](link_46).)

*   Any valid expression can now be used as a [decorator](link_47). Previously, the grammar was much more restrictive. See [**PEP 614**](link_4) for details. (Contributed by Brandt Bucher in [bpo-39702](link_48).)

*   Improved help for the [`typing`](link_49) module. Docstrings are now shown for all special forms and special generic aliases (like `Union` and `List`). Using [`help()`](link_39) with generic alias like `List[int]` will show the help for the correspondent concrete type (`list` in this case). (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40257](link_50).)

*   Parallel running of [`aclose()`](link_51) / [`asend()`](link_51) / [`athrow()`](link_51) is now prohibited, and `ag_running` now reflects the actual running status of the async generator. (Contributed by Yury Selivanov in [bpo-30773](link_52).)

*   Unexpected errors in calling the `__iter__` method are no longer masked by `TypeError` in the [`in`](link_51) operator and functions [`contains()`](link_12), [`indexOf()`](link_12) and [`countOf()`](link_12) of the [`operator`](link_12) module. (Contributed by Serhiy Storchaka in [bpo-40824](link_53).)

*   Unparenthesized lambda expressions can no longer be the expression part in an `if` clause in comprehensions and generator expressions. See [bpo-41848](link_54) and [bpo-43755](link_55) for details.

## New Modules[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#new-modules "Permalink to this headline")

## Summary – Release highlights[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#summary-release-highlights "Permalink to this headline")

New syntax features:

*   [**PEP 584**](link_2), union operators added to `dict`;

*   [**PEP 585**](link_3), type hinting generics in standard collections;

*   [**PEP 614**](link_4), relaxed grammar restrictions on decorators.

New built-in features:

*   [**PEP 616**](link_5), string methods to remove prefixes and suffixes.

New features in the standard library:

*   [**PEP 593**](link_6), flexible function and variable annotations;

*   [`os.pidfd_open()`](link_42) added that allows process management without races and signals.

Interpreter improvements:

*   [**PEP 573**](link_7), fast access to module state from methods of C extension types;

*   [**PEP 617**](link_8), CPython now uses a new parser based on PEG;

*   a number of Python builtins (range, tuple, set, frozenset, list, dict) are now sped up using [**PEP 590**](link_9) vectorcall;

*   garbage collection does not block on resurrected objects;

*   a number of Python modules (`_abc`, [`audioop`](link_10), `_bz2`, `_codecs`, `_contextvars`, `_crypt`, `_functools`, `_json`, `_locale`, [`math`](link_11), [`operator`](link_12), [`resource`](link_13), [`time`](link_14), `_weakref`) now use multiphase initialization as defined by PEP 489;

*   [**PEP 615**](link_23), the IANA Time Zone Database is now present in the standard library in the [`zoneinfo`](link_24) module;

*   [**PEP 602**](link_25), CPython adopts an annual release cycle.

### zoneinfo[¶](https://docs.python.org/3.9/whatsnew/3.9.html#zoneinfo "Permalink to this headline")
The [`zoneinfo`](https://docs.python.org/3.9/library/zoneinfo.html#module-zoneinfo "zoneinfo: IANA time zone support") module brings support for the IANA time zone database to the standard library. >>> from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo  
>>> from datetime import datetime, timedelta
